_note: Style conventions, not science. Scores are 0-1 (1 = best). Edit freely: frame names must match the frame shapes in the catalog. The 'pairings' sentences are shown to the shopper as the reason for a match.

oval.label: Oval
oval.summary: Balanced proportions: a little longer than wide, with a softly rounded jaw.
oval.principle: Almost any frame works on an oval face, so choose by style rather than correction.

round.label: Round
round.summary: Face length and cheekbone width are close, with full cheeks and a soft jaw.
round.principle: Angular frames add definition and make a round face look longer.

square.label: Square
square.summary: A strong jaw and a forehead of similar width, with fairly straight sides.
square.principle: Curved frames soften angles and balance a strong jawline.

heart.label: Heart
heart.summary: A wider forehead and cheekbones narrowing to a slim chin.
heart.principle: Frames that are light on top or wider at the bottom balance a narrow chin.

oblong.label: Oblong
oblong.summary: Noticeably longer than wide, with a long straight cheek line.
oblong.principle: Wide, deep frames add width and make a long face look shorter.

wayfarer.label: Wayfarer
wayfarer.summary: Slightly angled acetate frames, wider across the top. Bold and timeless.

rectangle.label: Rectangle
rectangle.summary: Wider than tall, with straight edges. Sharp and structured.

square.label: Square
square.summary: As tall as they are wide, with firm corners. Strong and graphic.

round.label: Round
round.summary: Circular lenses with no corners. Soft, retro and artistic.

oval.label: Oval
oval.summary: Gently curved lenses a little wider than tall. Easy and flattering.

cat-eye.label: Cat-eye
cat-eye.summary: Outer corners sweep upwards to lift the face. Confident and feminine.

aviator.label: Aviator
aviator.summary: Large teardrop lenses in a thin metal frame. Classic and light.

geometric.label: Geometric
geometric.summary: Faceted and hexagonal shapes with distinctive edges. Fashion-forward.

oval.wayfarer: Classic wayfarers sit neatly on balanced proportions and keep your natural symmetry.
oval.rectangle: Clean rectangular lines add a crisp, modern edge without upsetting your balance.
oval.square: Square lenses add a graphic edge, and an oval face carries the corners easily.
oval.round: Round lenses echo your soft curves for an easy, harmonious look.
oval.oval: Oval lenses mirror the shape of your face and keep everything in proportion.
oval.cat-eye: The upswept corners lift balanced features and add some personality.
oval.aviator: The teardrop shape suits balanced faces and never overwhelms them.
oval.geometric: An oval face can carry bold facets, which makes this a good way to stand out.

round.wayfarer: The angled top line adds structure and makes a round face look a little longer.
round.rectangle: Wide, straight lines give a round face the definition it lacks and lengthen it.
round.square: Firm corners contrast with soft curves and add definition across the cheeks.
round.round: Round lenses repeat your curves, so the effect is soft but adds little definition.
round.oval: Soft oval lenses are gentle on a round face but add little definition.
round.cat-eye: Upswept corners draw the eye up and out, which helps lift fuller cheeks.
round.aviator: The straight brow bar adds some definition, though the teardrop is fairly soft.
round.geometric: Faceted edges break up round contours and add welcome angles.

square.wayfarer: The strong top line repeats the angles of your jaw. It works, but it is a bold look.
square.rectangle: Straight lines echo a square jaw and can make the lower face look heavier.
square.square: Square on square doubles the angles, so expect a very strong look.
square.round: Round lenses soften a strong jaw and balance angular features.
square.oval: Oval lenses add curves where your face has angles, for a softer balance.
square.cat-eye: Upswept curves soften the jawline and lift the face.
square.aviator: The curved teardrop softens a strong jaw while keeping the look sharp.
square.geometric: Faceted shapes can compete with a strong jaw; rounded versions work best.

heart.wayfarer: A heavy top line adds weight to a forehead that is already your widest point.
heart.rectangle: Straight lines are neutral on a heart-shaped face but do little to balance the chin.
heart.square: Strong corners emphasise the forehead. A lighter frame would balance better.
heart.round: Round lenses soften a wide forehead and bring balance to a narrow chin.
heart.oval: Soft, light oval lenses balance a wide forehead and a narrow chin.
heart.cat-eye: The upswept line adds lift but also width on top, so a lighter frame works best.
heart.aviator: A teardrop is wider at the bottom, which balances a narrower chin.
heart.geometric: Heavy angular shapes add more weight to the top of the face.

oblong.wayfarer: Wide, deep frames add width and make a long face look shorter.
oblong.rectangle: A shallow rectangle can make a long face look longer. Deeper frames work better.
oblong.square: Tall square lenses add width and shorten the length of the face.
oblong.round: Round lenses add width and soften a long face.
oblong.oval: A shallow oval can make a long face look longer. Deeper lenses balance better.
oblong.cat-eye: Upswept corners add width at the cheekbones and balance a long face.
oblong.aviator: Large aviators add width and cover more of the mid-face.
oblong.geometric: Wide angular shapes add interest across the cheeks without adding length.
